title: Ignition scenarios, design fires and fire classes for Topologic Studio Next

conventions.shares: Fractions (0.49 = 49 %). 'share' is the share of fires, 'shareDeaths' the share of civilian deaths, both in the population named in 'of'. Values marked derived in 'note' are products of two published shares (scenario share = cause share x conditional share) or quotients computed here.
conventions.growth: Keys match zone.js GROWTH: slow, medium, fast, ultra-fast. alpha_kW_per_s2 is the class value (FD-02 in fire-equations-verified-2026-10-27.json); zone.js uses 0.188 for ultra-fast, 1055/75^2 = 0.1876.
conventions.measuredAlpha: Where a test reports a peak HRR Q_p (kW) and a time to peak t_p (s), the effective coefficient Q_p / t_p^2 is given as derivedAlpha and mapped to the nearest class on a log scale (class boundaries at the geometric means 0.00586, 0.0234 and 0.0938 kW s^-2). t_p includes any incubation after the test ignition, so derivedAlpha is a lower bound on the growth after sustained flaming.
conventions.peak: peak_kW is the Q_user that Studio's two-zone model takes; zone.js caps it at the ventilation limit 1500 A_o sqrt(H_o). peak_kW_per_m2, where given instead, is multiplied by the fire room's floor area (rooms.js floorArea).
conventions.basis: item = the first item alone; item+adjacent = the first item plus the furniture item it ignites (composite, a judgement); room = a measured room-scale test; occupancy = a standard's occupancy design fire.
conventions.evidence: Strongest evidence behind the scenario: peer-reviewed, standard, official statistics, industry statistics (NFPA), measurement (laboratory report or database). evidenceDetail says which field rests on what.
conventions.nameRegex: JavaScript regular expressions, flag 'i'. English tokens are preceded by (?:^|[^a-z]) rather than \b, because Revit-exported names start with prefixes such as 'M_' or 'N_' and '_' is a word character, so \b fails in 'M_Bed'. German and Norwegian tokens have no leading boundary so that compounds (Doppelbett, Elektroherd) match. Arabic tokens in nameHintsAr and spaceHintsAr are matched as substrings, because JavaScript \w and \b cover ASCII only. Apply nameExclude after nameRegex. Patterns were tested against the local IFC corpus on 2026-11-05 (review, section 5.3).
conventions.fireClass: NFPA 10 (2022) class of the fire at origin: A, B, C, D or K. For class C (energised equipment) fuelClass is the class of what burns once the equipment is involved. isoClass is the ISO 3941:2007 / EN 2:1992+A1:2004 class (A, B, C gases, D, F); 'L' marks ISO 3941:2026's new lithium-ion class.

occupancyDesignFires.note: EN 1991-1-2:2002 Annex E, Table E.5 (growth, RHR_f) and Table E.4 80 % fractile fire load, read as reproduced on a JRC Eurocodes workshop slide (jrc2012vassart, slide 22). Values apply with delta_q2 = 1.0.

secondItemIgnition.envelope: Irradiance measured 0.05 m from the fastest-burning furniture items reached about 80 kW/m2; 40 kW/m2 was not recorded farther than 0.44 m and 20 kW/m2 not beyond 0.88 m, so common furnishings needing about 20 kW/m2 'would stand little hazard of fire involvement if placed at least 1 m away' (pre-flashover only).

ignitionDistanceAtPeakMassLoss47gps_m.note: read by eye from Fig. 13 at the largest first item (47 g/s)

secondItemIgnition.pointSource: q'' = chi_r Q / (4 pi R^2) at R >= 5 D (TN 2133 Eq. 5, after Modak); chi_r measured 0.44 for corn oil and 0.37 for gasoline pan fires.

A.label: Ordinary combustibles
A.nfpa10: Wood, cloth, paper, rubber and many plastics (NFPA 10, 5.2.1).

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Average effective heat of combustion of wood-framed upholstered chairs and sofas, 13.9-20.9 MJ/kg (a polypropylene-framed chair 35.1 MJ/kg); wardrobes 14.2-17.5 MJ/kg. Wood pallets 14.0 MJ/kg (secondary).

co.note: Generic: below 0.01 kg/kg well ventilated (equivalence ratio below 0.5), about 0.2 kg/kg above an equivalence ratio of about 1.5; 0.05 at stoichiometric.

soot.note: Wood 0.015-0.018; flexible polyurethane foam 0.188; polystyrene foam 0.194 (Klote and Milke 2002, reproducing Tewarson; secondary). Furniture items measured 0.1-10.7 % particulate conversion at peak.

coToSootRatio.note: Well-ventilated CO/smoke yield ratio for ordinary polymers, liquids and gases; not for halogenated polymers.

growth.note: Occupancy default for dwellings, offices, schools and hospital rooms (EN 1991-1-2). Upholstered furniture alone is fast (derived 0.025-0.055 kW s^-2 for polyurethane-foam chairs and sofas).

ignition.note: 20 kW/m2 is Babrauskas's 'normal ignition range' for furnishings (10 especially easy, 40 difficult); most fabric/polyurethane items ignited within 45 s at 20 kW/m2. Piloted ignition of 12.7 mm plywood and 25 mm flexible foam: 16 kW/m2 and 390 C (SFPE guide, secondary).

embers.note: Charring solids (wood, structures, vegetation) produce firebrands; the evidence concerns outdoor fire spread, abstract-level only. Thermoplastic furnishings: no evidence either way.

suitable: foam (AFFF, FFFP) rated for class A

unsuitable.reason: Listed for classes B and C only; short range (about 1-2.4 m) and no cooling of deep-seated embers.

B.label: Flammable and combustible liquids and gases
B.isoNote: ISO 3941 / EN 2 split this into B (liquids and liquefiable solids) and C (gases).
B.nfpa10: Flammable liquids, combustible liquids, petroleum greases, tars, oils, oil-based paints, solvents, lacquers, alcohols and flammable gases (NFPA 10, 5.2.2).
examples: natural gas and LPG at burners and boilers

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Gasoline 44.1 and n-heptane 44.6 MJ/kg (TN 2133 Table 3, read). Range from methanol 20.0 to transformer oil 46.0 MJ/kg (SFPE Handbook 3rd ed. pool table via NUREG-1805 Suppl. 1, secondary).

co.note: Derived: CO yield = 0.034 g/m2 x SEA with gasoline SEA 0.65 m2/g (TN 2133 abstract and Eq. 18 relation).

soot.note: Derived: soot yield = 0.11 g/m2 x SEA (TN 2133 Eq. 18) with gasoline SEA 0.65 m2/g (+/- 45 %), pan fires 9.7-26 cm.

poolBurning.formula: m'' = mInf (1 - exp(-kBeta D)); Q = m'' deltaHc A

otherPools.columns: mInf kg m^-2 s^-1, kBeta m^-1 (null: no diameter dependence), deltaHc MJ/kg

growth.note: Pool values from the SFPE Handbook (3rd ed.) table derived from Babrauskas (1983), read in NUREG-1805 Suppl. 1 spreadsheets (secondary). 'Ultra-fast' for a spill is a judgement: a pool reaches its burning rate within seconds; it is not a fitted t-squared value.

ignition.note: Flash and autoignition temperatures of gasoline and solvents were not read in this study; a liquid at or above its flash point ignites from a pilot flame.

embers.note: No literature found on firebrands from liquid pools; inference, not a sourced finding.

suitable: foam (AFFF, FFFP), which floats on the fuel and prevents re-ignition
for pressurised gas or liquid jets: dry chemical, and only once the fuel supply can be shut off

unsuitable.reason: Water extinguishers are for class A only; a stream splashes and spreads burning liquid, and drops sinking into a hot liquid boil and expel it.

C.label: Energised electrical equipment
C.isoNote: ISO 3941:2007 and EN 2 have no electrical class; the fire is classed by its fuel (A or B).
C.nfpa10: Fires that involve energised electrical equipment (NFPA 10, 5.2.3).

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Mean of the average effective heats of combustion of free-burning TV sets (29.5), washing machines (32.3), dishwashers (31.3) and refrigerator-freezers (28.1); in a cupboard 18.6-19.5 MJ/kg.

co.note: Mean of the average CO yields per appliance type (TV 0.071, washing machine 0.038, dishwasher 0.067, refrigerator-freezer 0.049 kg/kg).

soot.note: Mean of the average smoke yields (TV 0.116, washing machine 0.021, dishwasher 0.036, refrigerator-freezer 0.050 kg/kg).

yields.hydrogenHalides: HF 27 g (2 g/kg of mass burnt, 193 g/kg of the 140 g of refrigerant) from one refrigerator-freezer; HCl 67-123 g from a dishwasher and a refrigerator-freezer; no HBr in any test.

growth.note: Judgement: appliances span slow (refrigerator-freezers, derived about 0.004-0.006 kW s^-2) to fast (TV sets, derived about 0.03-0.07 kW s^-2) after an incipient phase of 1.5-3 min (TV) to 10-20 min (washing machines). Use the item's own entry where one exists.

ignition.note: Ignition is by overheating, arcing or overload inside the equipment; not a radiant-flux criterion. Babrauskas's SFPE chapter on electrical fires (verified DOI) was not read.

embers.note: Plastics-dominated appliances; no evidence of firebrands. Inherits the fuel's behaviour.

suitable: dry chemical (but its residue can form a conductive path on wet equipment)
de-energise the circuit as soon as possible, then treat as class A or B

unsuitable.agent: water or foam on energised equipment
unsuitable.reason: Conducts electricity to the operator; NFPA 10 requires that class C extinguishers contain no conductive agent.

D.label: Combustible metals
D.nfpa10: Magnesium, titanium, zirconium, sodium, lithium and potassium (NFPA 10, 5.2.4).
examples: magnesium alloy parts and swarf (workshops, laboratories)

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Derived for magnesium: 601.60 kJ/mol (CODATA enthalpy of formation of MgO) / 24.305 g/mol.

co.note: Metal fires form metal oxide fume ('dense white smoke' for magnesium), not soot or CO from the metal itself.

growth.note: No t-squared characterisation found; out of scope for the two-zone model.

ignition.note: Magnesium autoignition about 473 C (alloys 427-650 C); sodium about 121 C; lithium about 179 C (secondary: NOAA CAMEO Chemicals and studies quoted in Zhao et al. 2022).

embers.note: Not established in the sources read.

suitable: dry sand, dolomite, soda ash, sodium chloride or graphite powder applied gently so the metal does not scatter

unsuitable.reason: Reacts with burning metal to release hydrogen; the reaction can be explosive (sodium and lithium react with water even cold).
Burning magnesium continues to react with them (secondary source).

K.label: Cooking oils and fats in cooking appliances
K.nfpa10: Cooking appliances that involve combustible cooking media (vegetable or animal oils and fats) (NFPA 10, 5.2.5).
examples: oil or fat in a pan on a cooktop
grease in an oven or range hood

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Corn oil, measured by a testing laboratory (TN 2133 Table 3).

co.note: Derived: 0.034 g/m2 x SEA with corn oil SEA 0.63 m2/g (+/- 22 %).

soot.note: Derived: 0.11 g/m2 x 0.63 m2/g (TN 2133 Eq. 18). CO and soot yields fall with pan diameter.

growth.note: Kitchen-scale: small cooktop fires 'spread and grew ultra-fast' in a 3.6 m x 3.4 m x 2.4 m kitchen with fiberboard cabinets (abstract). The pan fire alone peaks at 20-35 kW (28 cm pans) to 110 kW (26 cm pan, 7 mm of corn oil), 20-40 s after ignition.

ignition.note: Corn oil must exceed about 392 C to autoignite (TN 2133 citing Hamins et al.); oil temperature just before ignition in a cast-iron pan on a ceramic hob: canola 385 +/- 27, sunflower 392 +/- 29, olive 420 +/- 39, butter 429 +/- 18 C. Mean ignition after 309 +/- 81 s of heating, probability 0.44 +/- 0.13.

embers.note: No literature found on firebrands from oil fires; boil-over can throw burning oil, which is a spill, not an ember. Inference.

suitable: wet chemical (saponifies the oil into a foam blanket that excludes air and cools it)
fine water mist from fixed systems (cools the oil below autoignition)

unsuitable.reason: Drops sink into the hot oil, boil and expel it, spreading the fire.
Knocks the flame down but does not cool the oil below its autoignition temperature, so it re-ignites.

unsuitable.agent: wet chemical injected below the oil surface
unsuitable.reason: Can cause a reaction NFPA 10 compares to an explosion.

L.label: Lithium-ion cells and batteries (no metallic lithium)
L.note: Not an NFPA 10 class and not class D (which covers lithium metal). ISO 3941:2026 adds Class L (reported by trade and consultancy sources; the standard's text was not read). For NFPA purposes Studio records a charging pack as class C with fuel class B (electrolyte vapour) and A (the vehicle or device).

heatOfCombustion_MJ_per_kg.note: Not a single fuel; heat release scales with stored energy and state of charge.

yields.note: Seven commercial cell types; water mist also tested.

growth.note: An overcharged e-scooter in a closed bedroom: gas ignition about 20 s and flashover within 30 s of visible smoke (FSRI summary of a peer-reviewed paper whose abstract was read). An overcapacity e-bike pack alone: peak 68 kW at 80 % and 107 kW at 60 % state of charge, with jet flames.

ignition.note: Thermal runaway onset at 300 C for the e-bike packs tested (abstract).

embers.note: Packs eject burning material in jet flames, but no source read quantifies it.

agents.note: No peer-reviewed comparison of agents was read; ISO 3941:2026 is reported not to prescribe agents. Packs re-ignite without sustained cooling (abstract-level).

ranking.score: score_i = w_s x m_i / N_s, where w_s is the scenario's share of deaths in the dataset for the building's occupancy (frequency x consequence: share of fires x deaths per fire is proportional to share of deaths), m_i the match confidence of candidate i, and N_s the number of candidates matched to scenario s in the model.

ranking.occupancy: Residential: shareDeaths (US NFPA 2019-2023), with shareUK as a cross-check. Non-residential: shareNonResidential where given, else the scenario's residential value times 0.5 and flagged. The panel lets the user override the inferred occupancy.

corpusCheck.corpus: Local IFC test corpus (ifc-samples folder, local testing only; not in the repository): 45 distinct building models of at least 50 kB (one byte-identical duplicate removed).
findings: 17 of 45 models contain at least one element that the nameRegex patterns recognise: 10 an appliance, heater, fireplace or distribution board, 13 upholstered furniture, beds or desks.

No model contains an IfcElectricAppliance occurrence. IfcElectricApplianceType occurs in two IFC2x3 Revit exports (dental_clinic, Office_A) with PredefinedType NOTDEFINED and names such as '2000 lbs' and '3500 lbs', i.e. lift cars: the entity alone is not evidence of an appliance.

Appliances are exported as IfcBuildingElementProxy (Miele cooktop, oven, microwave, dryer, washer, fridge-freezer and dishwasher in Ifc4_Revit_ARC; 'M_Cook Top-4 Unit' and 'M_Refrigerator' in BasicHouse; 'N_Oven-Built-in' and 'Dishwasher:Asko oppvaskmaskin' in a Norwegian school), as IfcFlowTerminal ('M_Washing Machine' in BasicHouse), or as furniture types ('Refrigerator 24' and 'Cabinet Base Cooktop+Oven 24' in S_Office; 'Underbench oven 4D' in ISSUE_126).
All 238 IfcFurniture occurrences have PredefinedType unset or NOTDEFINED; only one IfcFurnitureType (Klassiqua office, DESK) is typed.
The only typed ignition-class entities with a specific PredefinedType are 44 IfcSpaceHeater RADIATOR and 2 IfcBoiler WATER in one model (TalTech), both hydronic.
Distribution boards appear only as proxies named 'Lighting and Appliance Panelboard'.
